title: Ancient Trees in Denmark: Cities to Explore
meta_description: Copenhagen's remarkable trees come with tape measurements, working names and a paper trail going back to 1941. One city mapped, 13 trees.
intro: Copenhagen's remarkable trees come with tape measurements, which is rarer than it should be. The Danish dendrological society has surveyed them one by one and filed them under working names: a beech in Frederiksberg Have is registered as Bøgen ved Bådfarten, the beech by the boat trip, which makes it the easiest tree in the city to find. A honey locust has been on record since a gardening magazine featured it in 1941. Assistens cemetery holds five of the thirteen mapped here, and the thickest tree inside its walls is a sycamore, the least exotic species in it. The oldest of the thirteen is the mulberry at Proviantgarden, the one tree anyone can still point to from Christian IV's attempt at a Danish silk industry. Thirteen trees, one city so far.
